question.worked_solution:
Remember that integration is the opposite of differentiation. So, if ${F}^{′}(x)=f(x),$ then integrating both sides of this equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(x) & =f(x) \\ \int {F}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x & =\int f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ F(x) & =\int f(x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}={x}^{-3/2}.$ So, we can use the power rule with $n=-\frac{3}{2}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x) & =\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {x}^{-3/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-3/2+1}}{(-\frac{3}{2}+1)}+C \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-1/2}}{(-\frac{1}{2})}+C \\  & =-2{x}^{-1/2}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
